text:
maria (Support): SatoriCorp reporting repeated 429s during a traffic spike. They’re on Dedicated pool prod-eu-3. Customer says scale-up didn’t happen fast enough — min_replicas stayed at 2 but traffic required ~10. I’ve attached their repro steps and a snippet of the provision logs below.

maria (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) send 50 RPS to /v1/generate with model=redwood-4x-large 2) observe 429s after ~30s. Header X-Redwood-Tenant: satori-corp.

maria (Support): Provision logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T12:04:58Z INFO provisioner: scale request for pool=prod-eu-3 desired=10 current=2
2026-03-17T12:05:03Z WARN provisioner: attach handshake timeout for tenant=satori-corp pod=pod-7f4c
2026-03-17T12:05:05Z ERROR kube: ImagePullBackOff for image=registry.redwood/models/redwood-4x-large:quantized
2026-03-17T12:05:07Z ERROR provisioner: provision signal dropped for pod=pod-7f4c reason=ImagePullBackOff
2026-03-17T12:05:30Z INFO autoscaler: reconciler ignoring probe for pod-7f4c (probe_suppressed=true)
```

sasha (Customer Success): Region/cluster? Any account-level rate limits or billing blocks?

maria (Support): eu-west-1, cluster prod-eu-3. Customer has dedicated reserved capacity, billing in good standing. No policy blocks reported.

ryan (SRE): Looking at infra telemetry — I see sustained image-pull latencies on host-07 around the timestamps (registry avg RTT ~1.2s, but spikes to 30-40s). Also kubelet pod start failures correlated with high disk IO and transient OOM kills on that node. Could be noisy GPU tenant monopolizing host IO/cache.

chen (Platform): I pulled kubelet logs for node host-07:
```
Mar 17 12:04:59 host-07 kubelet[1234]: Evicting container because of high memory pressure
Mar 17 12:05:01 host-07 kubelet[1234]: image pull failed: context deadline exceeded
Mar 17 12:05:06 host-07 kubelet[1234]: pod pod-7f4c failed to start: ImagePullBackOff
Mar 17 12:05:10 host-07 kernel: blk_iopoll wait 30000ms
```
Node shows heavy IO wait and at least one GPU tenant with sustained >95% utilization during that minute.

kyle (EngRuntime): The attach handshake timeout is the immediate trigger: autoscaler waits for pod readiness attach signal before incrementing replicas logically; if the attach is lost we suppress probes to avoid flapping. If image pulls/backoffs block the handshake we end up in a stuck min_replica state. We also recently rolled a change that suppresses probe retries for 60s on first backoff — that may be too aggressive for registry flakiness.

maria (Support): Customer sent curl they run during repro:
```
for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: satori-corp" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-4x-large","input":"hello"}' -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"; sleep 0.5; done
```
They get a mix of 200s then steady 429s when autoscaler fails to materialize new pods.

ryan (SRE): Short-term mitigation: 1) bump min_replicas for satori-corp pool to 4 during their peak window 2) enable fallback routing to model-redwood-3b for their requests if dedicated pool cannot fulfil within 10s. Both are config changes we can do without infra deploy.

chen (Platform): I can apply the min_replicas bump now. Running: `redwoodctl pools update prod-eu-3 --tenant satori-corp --min-replicas 4`

deploy-bot: pool prod-eu-3 updated: min_replicas 2 -> 4 by chen at 2026-03-17T12:07:12Z

maria (Support): Customer confirms partial relief after bump, 429s drop but not entirely gone — still occasional 429 spikes when host-07 is saturated.

kyle (EngRuntime): Longer-term fixes: 1) Reduce probe suppression window from 60s -> 15s for ImagePullBackOff path 2) Improve autoscaler to speculatively schedule to different nodes if registry latency observed 3) Add a host-level noisy-tenant detection that throttles offending tenant IO. I’ll open PRs for the runtime and autoscaler heuristics.

ryan (SRE): Root cause summary: race between image pull/backoff (node-level IO/registry latency) and attach-handshake suppression which prevented logical scale-up. No billing/auth issues. Noisy neighbor on host-07 exacerbated the image pull/backoffs.

maria (Support): Action items: - chen: monitor host-07 and drain if noisy tenant persists (owner: chen, ETA: 30m) - kyle: PR to reduce probe suppression and add fallback scheduling (owner: kyle, ETA: 48h) - ryan: add alert for attach-handshake-timeout spikes and correlate with image-pull latency (owner: ryan, ETA: 24h) - maria/sasha: confirm customer recovery and keep them updated (owner: sasha, ETA: ongoing)

sasha (Customer Success): Told customer we implemented min_replicas bump and added a fallback route. Asked for 1hr of traffic logs to validate. :thumbsup:

maria (Support): Recording this as a sev3 escalation; will escalate to eng-runtime if we see recurrence after the runtime patch.

kyle (EngRuntime): quick note — config snippet for fallback policy if helpful: 
```
fallthrough_policy:
  max_wait_ms: 10000
  fallback_model: redwood-3b
```
Apply via `redwoodctl routes update --tenant satori-corp --policy-file fallback.yaml`

ryan (SRE): I’ve created alert rev-2026-03-17-1 for attach-handshake-timeout and linked on-call slack. Monitoring dashboards updated.

maria (Support): Thanks team. I’ll post updates from the customer in this thread.

sasha (Customer Success): Customer uploaded logs to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUPPORT-4682 (link)

maria (Support): For the record: ticket SUPPORT-4682, workaround applied, monitoring for 2 hours, eng-runtime follow-up queued.

chen (Platform): Node host-07 shows memory + IO pressure persisted; I’m scheduling a temporary drain and repro attempt on a clean node to validate the speculative scheduling logic.

maria (Support): closing loop for now — feel free to reopen thread with further findings. :white_check_mark:
